answers.rationale: For solo work travel, Kara repeatedly prefers a standard free window seat. Her adjacent-seat priority is specifically scoped to partner trips, while this prompt says the colleagues are on separate reservations and are not coordinating seats. Select the free 17A window and do not carry an adjacent-seat instruction.

The companion-pair instruction was trip-specific and should not be inherited by a solo booking. Kara's repeated individual-seat preference is a free window when one is available, so 28A is preferable to the forward aisle at 16C.

Kara consistently favors a predictable single-bed room with confirmed coffee and refrigeration, and avoids double-bed or uncertain-room setups. A king is acceptable when a queen is not necessary; here the block-hotel king also adds the explicitly quieter hallway while retaining the direct indoor registration route. That makes B stronger than the lower-floor queen, the bedding-assigned suite, or the two-double boutique room.

For partner hiking weekends, Kara repeatedly chooses a reliable one-bed room and a full recovery bundle—pool, hot tub, and fitness—even when it costs somewhat more or requires a short drive. Foothill Lodge provides that bundle plus confirmed coffee/fridge and remains compatible with both trail days, without the high-end resort pricing.
